related_questions.question: How does a vaccine work step by step?

text_blocks.snippet: Vaccines work by mimicking an infection to stimulate the body's immune system to develop protection (immunity) against a specific disease. This process involves introducing a weakened or inactive version of the disease-causing agent (antigen) into the body, prompting the immune system to produce antibodies and other protective cells.

list.title: 1. Introduction of the Antigen:
list.snippet: A vaccine contains an antigen, which could be a weakened or inactivated form of a virus or bacteria, or a specific part of it.

list.title: 2. Immune System Activation:
list.snippet: When the antigen enters the body, the immune system recognizes it as a foreign substance and begins to respond.

list.title: 3. Antibody Production:
list.snippet: The immune system produces antibodies, specialized proteins that bind to and neutralize the specific antigen.

list.title: 4. Memory Cell Development:
list.snippet: The immune system also develops memory cells, which are long-lasting immune cells that "remember" the antigen. If the body encounters the actual disease-causing organism later, these memory cells can quickly trigger a stronger and faster immune response, preventing or reducing illness.

list.title: 5. Immunity:
list.snippet: This process leads to immunity, meaning the body is now prepared to fight off the actual disease if encountered in the future.
